summary: The B10 is Leapmotor's small electric SUV, sold in Australia from $37,888 list in two pure-battery grades that undercut the BYD Atto 3, Geely EX5 and Kia EV3. Australian reviewers are unusually united on the chassis — carsales scored it 81/100 and CarsGuide 7.4/10, both crediting the rear-drive layout and Maserati-influenced suspension tune with more composure than anything else at the price, and CarPlay and Android Auto fix the omission that dogged the related C10. Where they part company is how much the rough edges cost it: the standard Linglong tyres, the intrusive lane-keep system and the touchscreen-only controls drew criticism from every outlet, and the B10 is also sold here as a range-extender under the same two badges, so a buyer has to check which powertrain a quote refers to.
pros: Cheapest way into a new electric SUV in Australia at $37,888 list, several thousand under a BYD Atto 3 Essential and a Geely EX5 Complete, with a 14.6-inch screen, panoramic roof, wireless charging and 360-degree cameras standard on the base Style

Rear-wheel drive with Maserati-influenced suspension tuning — carsales rated it 'one of the best value and most engaging small electric SUVs' at 81/100 and CarsGuide gave 7.4/10, both singling out ride and handling as ahead of the class
Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are fitted, unlike the Leapmotor C10, which still has neither on any grade
The $40,888 Design LR steps up to a 67.1kWh pack, 434km WLTP and 168kW DC charging (30-80% in about 18 minutes) against the Style's 56.2kWh and 140kW, for $3,000
Eight years of capped-price servicing at roughly $370 per visit on 12-month/20,000km intervals, plus eight years of roadside assistance and a five-star ANCAP rating
cons: Not rated to tow at all — braked capacity is 0kg on both electric grades, where the B10 range-extender is rated to 750kg and the larger Leapmotor C10 manages 1,500kg

Standard Linglong eco tyres were criticised by RACQ, carsales and CarsGuide alike for squealing and losing grip early under brakes, which reviewers say squanders the chassis the car is otherwise praised for
Lane-keep assist is intrusive enough that multiple Australian reviewers disable it every drive, and there are no physical controls — mirrors, vents and most functions live in the touchscreen
Six-year/150,000km warranty is unconditional but trails the seven years offered by Kia, MG, Geely and Chery in the same price bracket, after Leapmotor cut the term from seven years for MY25
Resale is the open risk: Leapmotor has around 20 Australian dealers, almost no local resale history, and launched the B10 on a $38,990 national drive-away offer that sat below the true on-road cost
